subject: Mutual acceptance runbook, quality gates & trigger matrix for QuantaFlow evaluation

Subject: Draft: mutual acceptance runbook and test matrix for upcoming eval

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As promised I pulled together a compact runbook that frames the evaluation as a series of measurable checkpoints rather than a single pass/fail gate. The goal is to make the close timeline predictable for both teams. Attached is a first draft (redwood-qflow-eval-runbook-v1.pdf) and a companion test-case spreadsheet.

High-level proposal (TL;DR):
- Week 0: Kickoff + data connectivity check (ingest sample, keys, SSO test)
- Week 1: Smoke throughput & latency verification (95th pct target under representative load)
- Week 2: Quality spot checks on 3 canonical flows + automated eval suite
- Week 3: Failure-mode exercises (fallbacks, degraded-accuracy thresholds) + security questionnaire outputs
- Week 4: Executive sign-off (MAP close if gates met)

I called out explicit acceptance criteria in the PDF (SLO thresholds, pass counts for test cases, and allowed regressions). Two things we'd like from your side to firm this up:
1) Confirm the three canonical flows you want validated (e.g., user-search, triage-bot, summarization).
2) Confirm whether procurement needs a formal statement of work before week 2 testing begins.

If that plan looks reasonable I can loop in Karthik for the technical acceptance tests and Lauren for SLA/contract triggers.

Best,
Sofia

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@quantaflow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Technical acceptance test spec (summary)

Folks —

Attaching a concise summary here in-line; full spec is in the spreadsheet (qflow-test-cases.xlsx). Key points:

1) Baseline collection (Week 0): collect 1k representative queries across the three flows; compute baseline metrics (latency P50/P95, throughput per node, task-specific quality metrics).

2) Smoke/Throughput (Week 1): run 30-minute ramped test with target concurrent sessions = 75% of QuantaFlow's projected peak. Acceptance: P95 latency <= 420ms and error rate < 1.5%. If either threshold is missed, outcome = remediation sprint required (not an immediate fail).

3) Quality validation (Week 2): run the automated eval on the test spreadsheet; acceptance = at least 92% of the canonical examples meet task-specific thresholds (per-sheet column). We define a soft-fail band (85–91%) that requires joint remediation but can still allow a conditional MAP extension.

4) Failure-mode exercises (Week 3): run three simulated failure scenarios (node dropout, injected latency, corrupted prompt). Rollback trigger = observed mean-quality drop > 6% vs baseline across 300-sample window OR user-facing regression > 8% in a live canary (we capture canary footprint separately).

5) Evidence package: we will provide an artifacts bundle (run logs, perf traces, per-case eval outputs, and the security inventory) within 48 hours of each test window finishing.

Operational notes:
- We will use a deterministic seed for evaluators to avoid non-determinism drift.
- Any deviation that requires model weight changes triggers a new evaluation run (not accepted as remediation).

Happy to walk through the spec in a short session; recommend 30 minutes on Monday.

Karthik
Senior Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: SOW paragraph, price cap and MAP triggers (final)

Hi Emily / procurement —

Attached is the one-paragraph SOW for your procurement team and a short MAP trigger matrix below. Pricing note: smoke/throughput verification (Week 1) is covered under the evaluation credit; any extended load testing beyond the agreed window will be billed at our standard engineering rate (estimate capped at $4,000 unless you request additional capacity).

SOW (one paragraph): Redwood Inference will perform a four-week technical evaluation for QuantaFlow covering connectivity verification, performance benchmarks, automated quality validation on canonical examples, and failure-mode exercises. Deliverables include an evidence bundle after each test window, a short remediation plan for any soft-fails, and a final acceptance report to support internal approvals. Testing will be performed on a mutually agreed schedule; load testing will not commence until a signed SOW paragraph or procurement acknowledgement is received.

MAP trigger matrix (summary):
- Green: All acceptance criteria met -> MAP closed, proceed to order form
- Amber: Soft-fail band met (85–91%) or single non-critical perf miss -> joint remediation plan, 1-week extension
- Red: Hard fail (below 85% quality or P95 latency > 600ms or error rate > 3%) -> pause evaluation, technical remediation and re-baselining required

Next step from you: please confirm canonical example list and route procurement acknowledgement to procurement@quantaflow.com so we can schedule the kickoff. Once we have that I'll publish a calendar invite for the Week 0 kickoff (30 min).

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
